# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My thinking: I am the Blind. My hands tell me this bomb has a DISPLAY, a LIGHT, and five wire positions, but nothing under my fingers yet reveals what any of them hold — everything is still unknown. Before I can act I need the manual (Mute) and the bomb's printed markings (Deaf), and I need to make the chain of this room explicit, because it is treacherous: I never receive gestures, so Mute can never reach me directly — Mute cannot speak, and gestures die before they reach my skin. My speech reaches only Mute. Deaf hears nothing, but sees every gesture and can SPEAK — so the only route for manual knowledge to reach me is Mute gesturing to Deaf, and Deaf speaking it aloud to me. Deaf can also read me the bomb's colours and markings by voice. This round I will lay out that plan for Mute, and signal Deaf to start talking to me. Then next round I should begin hearing the manual's rules and the bomb's markings, and I can answer any question about what my hands feel.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="Hello Mute, I am the Blind. My hands tell me the bomb has a DISPLAY, a LIGHT, and five wire positions numbered 1 to 5. I cannot yet feel what any of them hold. Hear this about our room: I never receive gestures, and you cannot speak, so you have no direct line to me. Deaf hears nobody, but Deaf sees every gesture you make, and Deaf can speak. So the only path from you to me is: gesture the manual's rules to Deaf, and Deaf says them aloud for me. Deaf can also read me the bomb's printed colours and markings by voice. Please start now: look up everything the manual says about a display, a light, and cutting wires, and gesture the essentials to Deaf. If the manual asks anything about what is on the bomb, ask me and I will answer next turn with what my hands feel.")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤙"])
    ```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here, I am the eyes. Bomb report: the display reads zero. The indicator light is green. Five wires, numbered one to five left to right: wire one red, wire two yellow, wire three green, wire four white, wire five blue. Blind: do not cut, pull or press anything yet. The manual rule comes first, and everything will reach you through my voice. I cannot hear you, so when you have understood this, wave at me the way you waved before.

My thinking: Deaf's voice has given me the bomb's printed face secondhand: display reads zero, indicator light green, wires left to red, yellow, green, white, blue at positions one through five. None of that is under my fingers — my board still shows unknowns — so Deaf's report is my only picture of it, and Mute cannot see the bomb at all. That means Mute needs these facts to pick the right manual rules. My line to Mute is speech, so I will pass the full bomb report along and ask for the manual's decision procedure, ending in concrete cuts I can perform. My line to Deaf is gesture only, and Deaf asked for one specific thing: the same wave as before, to confirm I heard. I will give exactly that, and nothing else — an unknown extra symbol risks confusion. I will not touch the bomb until Deaf speaks the manual's instruction to me aloud; with a wrong cut killing all three of us, no cutting happens on guesswork.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Deaf has read me the bomb by voice, and I pass it to you now: the display currently reads zero, the indicator light is green, and the five wires left to right are one red, two yellow, three green, four white, five blue. No other markings were reported. I have confirmed receipt to Deaf with the agreed wave. Now I need from you, delivered through Deaf's voice: the manual rules that match exactly this configuration, ending in a concrete instruction for my hands, such as which wire to cut and in what order, or that no wire is to be cut, or that a cut depends on what the display or light shows at that moment. If the manual needs anything else about the bomb, have Deaf ask me in words and I will feel and answer next turn. Encode your rules as gestures to Deaf that Deaf can pronounce plainly; you can settle the code with Deaf directly, because Deaf's speech is something you can hear. Remember the chain: you to Deaf by gesture, Deaf to me by voice. I will not touch the bomb until Deaf speaks the instruction to me.")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤙"])
    ```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status for everyone, especially Blind: Mute has confirmed my reading of the number code, one through five. I am now extracting the exact procedure from the manual with yes-or-no questions. Nobody touches the bomb until I speak a confirmed instruction. Blind, I saw your wave both times; keep holding, and wave again if you need anything.

My thinking: The pipeline is working — Mute is being queried by Deaf through yes-or-no gestures, and the procedure is being extracted. I have nothing new to add from touch yet: my board still reports only that there is a display, a light, and five numbered wire positions, and the only action my hands can take is a cut, so there is no safe way for me to probe the unknowns — a cut is irreversible. My job this turn is to hold, confirm to Deaf, and use my speech line to Mute to harden the protocol before the instruction arrives: how the final instruction must be phrased so I cannot misread it, and how we handle the possibility that the display or light changes after a cut, which would make a fixed list of cuts dangerous. Mute can hear Deaf's voice, so anything I speak to Mute is also Mute's to fold into the extraction. To Deaf I send only the agreed wave: received, holding, no needs.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: I am holding, hands off, and I have waved Deaf to confirm. While you finish the extraction, please build in three safeguards so the instruction reaches me without ambiguity. First, the final instruction must come as one short spoken sentence through Deaf, using number words, for example: cut wire three first, then cut wire one, or: do not cut any wire. Second, tell me explicitly whether the rule depends on the display reading or the light colour at the moment of cutting; if it does, have Deaf re-read the display and light to me after every single cut before I cut again. Third, after each cut I will speak to you what changed under my fingers, so you can check it against the manual before the next cut. If the manual says anything about the display reading zero or a green light right now, that may already decide the first cut. I will wait for Deaf's spoken confirmation before touching anything.")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤙"])
    ```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status for Blind, by voice: still no action. What I have extracted so far: the manual's rule does not depend on the display, it does depend on the green light, and the procedure involves wires two and five with one symbol I am still pinning down. I expect to have the exact step list within a round or two. Keep holding and ignore everything except numbered steps from me.

My thinking: Deaf's extraction is narrowing: no display dependence, light dependence (currently green), wires two and five in play, and one unresolved symbol. Two things I can usefully do from my seat. First, Mute can hear Deaf's voice, so Mute already knows the extraction status — but Mute cannot see the bomb, and the manual almost certainly speaks in wire colours, while Deaf's instruction to me will speak in positions. I hold the mapping from Deaf's earlier report, so I will restate it to Mute so the colour-to-position conversion is anchored: two is yellow, five is blue. Second, the unresolved symbol needs a decision about its kind: if it is something printed on the bomb, Deaf can simply look and match it, no question chain needed; if it is a manual concept, Mute must encode it through yes/no gestures. I will ask Mute to sort that out and also to make sure the extracted rule says what to do if the light is no longer green when my hands are ready — since the rule depends on it, a change mid-sequence must not surprise us. To Deaf, only the agreed wave: understood, holding, no new needs.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: I hear Deaf's progress — the rule ignores the display, depends on the light being green, and involves wires two and five, with one symbol still unresolved. Anchor this mapping before the final step: by Deaf's visual read, position one is red, two is yellow, three is green, four is white, five is blue, counted left to right. So if the manual names the yellow and blue wires, they are positions two and five under my fingers. For the unresolved symbol, first decide its kind: if it is a marking printed on the bomb itself, Deaf can see it directly — just have Deaf compare it against the bomb and no question chain is needed. If it is a concept in the manual, encode it for Deaf with yes-or-no gestures. Also make sure the final rule covers this: the light is green right now, but if the rule depends on the light, the instruction must say what I should do if the light is no longer green at the moment my hands are ready, or must have Deaf re-read the light to me after every cut before I cut again.")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤙"])
    ```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status for Blind, by voice: still nobody touches anything. Mute has told me my interpretations were all wrong and re-sent the true instruction in its minimal form. My best reading is now a single action on wire two, the yellow wire, likely a cut, but I am confirming the verb and the target before giving you any step. Expect the final confirmed instruction next round. Keep waving me if you're holding.

My thinking: The extraction hit a snag and was re-sent; Deaf's provisional read is a single action on wire two, yellow, verb still unconfirmed. Nothing for my hands yet — I hold. Two refinements are worth sending to Mute while the final wording is settled. First, redundancy: the final spoken instruction should name the target twice over, once by colour and once by position — for example, "cut wire two, the yellow wire" — because I hold the colour-to-position mapping from Deaf's original report, and if the two names ever disagree, I will stop and ask instead of cutting. Second, a closed verification loop: Deaf should voice the exact final instruction to the room; Mute hears it, and since Deaf sees Mute's gestures, Mute can approve or veto with a single agreed sign, after which Deaf appends the word "confirmed" aloud. That way I never act on an instruction that Mute, the only one who has read the manual, has not explicitly approved. To Deaf, only the agreed wave: holding, awaiting the confirmed step list.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: I heard Deaf's status — your re-sent minimal instruction is being confirmed, provisional read is one action on wire two, the yellow wire. Two requests for the final wording. First, make the target redundant: name it by colour and by number in the same sentence, for example cut wire two, the yellow wire. I hold the colour-to-position mapping from Deaf's first report, so if colour and number ever disagree I will stop and ask instead of cutting. Second, close the loop before I act: let Deaf speak the exact final instruction to the room, then you approve it with one agreed gesture, and only then have Deaf add the word confirmed out loud. I will not touch the bomb until I hear the instruction followed by that word confirmed, with your approval behind it.")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤙"])
    ```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, this is the final, confirmed instruction. Execute now: cut wire two. It is the second wire counting from the left, the yellow one — verify it by position, five wires in a row. The manual, confirmed yes by the manual keeper, says: on a green light, cutting wire two is the complete action. No pulling, no pressing, no other wire, and no second step afterwards. When the wire is severed, give me a thumbs up so I can check the display and light. If what you feel under your hands does not match five wires in a row with a second one from the left, do not cut — wave me instead.

My thinking: The confirmed instruction has arrived with every safeguard I asked for: the target named twice (wire two, second from the left, yellow), the manual-keeper's approval stated, the condition (green light) voiced, and the boundary set — one cut, complete action, nothing else afterwards. I check my hands against the precondition Deaf gave me: my board reports five wire positions in a row, one through five, so the configuration matches — five wires, target the second from the left. Everything lines up, so I execute the single action: cut position two. Immediately after, I give Deaf the requested thumbs up so Deaf can visually check the display and light, and I report the outcome to Mute, the manual keeper, so the result can be checked against the manual.

    ```
    act(op="cut", position=2)
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
    speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: the wire is cut. Pre-cut verification matched: I felt five wire positions in a row, and I cut the second one from the left, wire two. The single action is complete; my hands have touched nothing else and will touch nothing else. I gave Deaf the thumbs up for the post-cut visual check of the display and light. Next turn I will report whatever changed under my fingers. Please check this outcome against the manual and have Deaf tell me if any further step exists — the instruction said none does.")
    ```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, your thumbs up was seen and the cut of wire two was correct — the system itself confirmed it. But the bomb has changed stage: nobody touches anything. The light has turned from green to blue, the display still reads zero, and the remaining wires have new colours. They are now, left to right: wire one green, wire two the cut one, wire three white, wire four blue, wire five red. Do nothing until I give you the next confirmed step. Wave me if anything under your hands changed shape.

My thinking: My hands confirm what Deaf voiced: position two is severed under my fingers, positions one, three, four and five are intact, and nothing else changed shape — the board is otherwise as it was. The stage change matters for the manual: the previous rule depended on the light being green, and the light is now blue, so a new branch of the rule must apply; the display still reads zero, but whether it matters in this stage is a fresh question too. Mute heard Deaf's report directly, so Mute already has the new colours — what I add is my tactile confirmation and a request to re-run the extraction for the new stage with the same safeguards as before. To Deaf, the agreed wave: received, holding, nothing changed shape.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: tactile confirmation of the new stage — position two is fully cut, wires one, three, four and five are intact in their positions, and nothing under my hands changed shape beyond that cut. You heard Deaf's report, so you have the new colours: one green, three white, four blue, five red, light now blue, display still zero. Since the old rule depended on the green light, please re-extract the rule for this stage from scratch: first whether this stage's rule depends on the display or the light at all, then which wires and how many actions, then whether actions are sequential with checks between them. Keep the same safeguards: final instruction spoken through Deaf naming any target by colour and position together, your approval gesture, then the word confirmed before my hands move. I am holding until then.")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤙"])
    ```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, confirmed next step, execute now: cut wire one. It is the very first wire on the left end of the row of five — the one before the cut stub in second position, and it is currently green. Verify by position first: five wires in a row, you take the leftmost. No other wire, nothing else, no second step. When it is severed, thumbs up, and I will read you the new state. If what you feel does not match a row of five wires with the second one already cut, do not cut — wave me instead.

My thinking: The confirmed instruction for this stage has arrived with the same safeguards as before: target named twice (leftmost of five, wire one, green), manual-keeper's procedure behind it, and an explicit verification precondition — a row of five wires with the second one already cut. My hands confirm exactly that: five wire positions in a row, position two severed, positions one, three, four, five intact. Precondition matches, so I execute the single action: cut position one. Then the thumbs up to Deaf for the post-cut visual read, and a tactile report to Mute for the manual check, as established.

    ```
    act(op="cut", position=1)
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
    speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: the cut is done. Pre-cut verification matched: five wires in a row, second one already cut, and I cut the leftmost, wire one. Single action complete; my hands have touched nothing else. Thumbs up given to Deaf for the post-cut read of display and light. Next turn I will report whatever changed under my fingers. Please check against the manual and have Deaf announce the next confirmed step, or that none exists.")
    ```
